analysis.title: Global Credit: What We're Watching
key_insights: Hotter-than-expected CPI last week reignited hawkish Fed repricing and sold off the rates curve, with markets pricing a full hike by December and three by June 2027. Credit spreads still tightened across regions.

US IG spreads tightened 4bp (0.29% excess return) and US HY tightened 20bp (0.65% excess return), led by BBs. Loans tightened 3bp. Flows were positive in all three: IG +$630mn, HY +$1.36bn, Loans +$910mn.

Core call: US IG curve to flatten near term. The next phase of AI capex shifts toward chips, which may bring more short-dated financing and front-end supply. Trailing 3-month issuance is about 47% front-end, and yield buyers support the long end.

Trade: long CDX IG 0-3% equity tranche versus the index, delta-hedged 1:8x, to position for compression in AI-related credit risk. Buying AI-name CDS protection was the earlier preferred bearish expression, but the AI basket has widened about 40bp in a month.
The AI CDS basket now trades more than 85bp wider than CDX IG, and the CDX IG equity tranche has sold off materially. Morgan Stanley prefers the tranche over single-name AI exposure.

Higher rates favor up-in-quality. Morgan Stanley moves from preferring HY over IG (held for most of the year because of IG supply) to liking HY vs IG decompression. The CDX HY/IG ratio is at three-year lows and CCCs have repriced sharply.
Risk in HY: further rate rises could spill from CCCs into parts of Single-Bs. A rates rally would help HY re-compress and hurt the decompression trade.

Europe: expects positive credit excess returns in 2027. Valuations are cheaper than the US and AI issuance overhang is smaller. EUR credit screens cheap to USD on a currency-hedged basis, and carry and roll-down are near decade highs. Central-bank tightening is expected to peak in 1Q.

Europe positioning: favors banks on fundamentals and valuations, with accelerating front-end supply as a risk. Removes the cautious autos stance held since mid-year. Stays cautious on real estate (rates sensitivity, policy tightening, German political uncertainty). Sees room for long-end high-quality paper to outperform and BBB curves as flat.

EUR IG tightened 5bp (0.24% excess return) with the curve bull-steepening. EUR IG issuance was €23bn, bringing YTD to €691bn (+1% y/y). Inflows (~$600mln) were concentrated in ETFs while mutual funds saw a seventh straight week of outflows.

EUR HY tightened 25bp, the largest weekly tightening since April 2025, for 0.84% excess return, led by Single Bs. EUR HY funds saw net outflows of $35m, skewed by the removal of one ~$500m target maturity fund. EUR HY supply was €5bn, YTD €130bn (-9% y/y).
Asia: Asia credit tightened 10bp and APAC credit 6bp. Asia HY (-34bp) outperformed Asia IG (-6bp). GOOGL priced its first HKD and SGD bonds, raising about USD 2bn and USD 1.8bn.
YTD US supply is $2080bn in IG (+22% y/y), $288bn in HY (-3% y/y) and $369bn in Loans (-10% y/y). US HY issuance last week was $2bn and Loans $9bn.

Sector dispersion in US IG: media and tech outperformed, autos and real estate lagged. In HY, telecom and media outperformed while autos and financial services lagged. Oracle bonds were the worst BBB performers (about 20-34bp wider MTD) and Charter bonds the best (about 38-55bp tighter).
Upcoming data: US retail sales forecast flat for October and UK CPI forecast at 3.65% y/y by Morgan Stanley economists.

trade_ideas.description: Long CDX IG 0-3% equity tranche versus the CDX IG index, delta-hedged 1:8x
trade_ideas.rationale: Expresses compression in AI-related credit risk through the broader market rather than single AI names after AI basket CDS widened about 40bp in a month.
trade_ideas.risk: Further deterioration in sentiment around AI names drives another leg wider in spreads and the equity tranche underperforms the index.

trade_ideas.description: CDX index decompression (HY vs IG), with an up-in-quality bias
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher rates reinforce the safe-haven status of US IG while sub-IG credit metrics are more vulnerable.
trade_ideas.risk: A rally in rates could lead to CDX HY outperforming IG.

trade_ideas.description: Expect US IG curve flattening (relative widening pressure at the front end)
trade_ideas.rationale: Hyperscaler issuance shifting to the front end and competing with chip financing needs makes sub-5Y paper less attractive.
trade_ideas.risk: Long-end hyperscaler or non-AI issuance surprises to the upside, or chip financing deals underwhelm.

trade_ideas.rationale: Vulnerable to policy tightening and political uncertainty in Germany.
trade_ideas.risk: A rally in rates could keep real estate spreads anchored and orderly.
